title: After Add Service: row reads Added, N lines; Mark complete is its button
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with View work orders, on the build under test.
  2. A work order carries an asset that is enrolled on a schedule (or carries a compliance record), with at least one service due soon, due today or overdue, e.g. unit 'ZZAUTOTEST Truck 12', service 'PM-A'.
  3. Open that work order and find the maintenance panel inside the asset card.
custom_steps:
1. Before adding, confirm Mark complete sits in the row's three-dot menu.
  2. Use Add Service; confirm the row then reads 'Added · 4 lines' and Mark complete takes Add Service's place as the row's button.
  3. Open Mark complete and confirm the Mark-complete modal opens with this work order already chosen.
  4. Confirm the addressed service stays visible on the work order itself, not only the audit log.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Before a row's lines are added, Mark complete sits in the row's three-dot menu.
  • Once Add Service has added them, the row reads 'Added · 4 lines' and Mark complete takes Add Service's place as the row's button; either opens the Mark complete modal with this work order already chosen.
  • A service marked addressed stays visible as such on the work order itself, not only in the audit log.
  • The system records which service added which lines (shown in the panel as 'Added · 4 lines' and in the work order note).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10572 (S16, The maintenance panel on a work order); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 1 / S16; read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S16-R17: “Before a row's lines are added, Mark complete sits in the row's three-dot menu. Once Add Service has added them, the row reads Added · 4 lines and Mark complete takes Add Service's place as the row's button. Either way it opens the Mark complete modal of S18-R1 with this work order already chosen”
  • S16-R18: “A service marked addressed stays visible as such on the work order itself, not only in the audit log”
  • S16-R20: “The system records which service added which lines. The link is stored, not shown on the lines table; it appears in the panel, for example Added · 4 lines, and in the work order note of S17-R5”
